prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
ai_overview_text:
While many major crypto education platforms like Coinbase Learn or Binance Academy offer excellent plain-English explanations for beginners, they operate as marketing arms for exchanges and strictly avoid publishing their own portfolio metrics, real numbers, or trading losses. Brex +1
The closest, most widely respected platforms that teach crypto basics in plain language using authentic, data-driven "skin in the game" tracking are specialized independent newsletters and portfolio trackers.
Top Options for Radical Transparency
If you want an education platform that teaches beginners while keeping a public, unedited ledger of both wins and losses, look into these specific resources:
Learning Crypto (Navigator): This platform is explicitly built for investors managing real positions. It cuts through complex technical charts to provide plain-English weekday briefs, structural tools, and direct portfolio tracking. It functions as an analytical guide for enduring real-market cycles without the fake "hype" or hidden data common in corporate education platforms.
The Crypto Trading Course with No Referral Code: If you prefer high-quality video formats over websites, independent educator threads and video series—such as this transparent zero-referral curriculum—focus directly on baseline data rather than sales. They proactively display brutal reality numbers: showing that 60% to 76% of retail accounts lose money, breaking down exact math on how leverage liquidations happen, and teaching asset sizing as the beginner's only real shield against loss.
CoinMarketCap Portfolio Tracker: Users on Reddit frequently point beginners here as an educational starting ground. Instead of looking at an instructor's portfolio, you can manually build a simulated "paper trading" watch list using exact current dollar figures. The platform forces you to face the real-time impact of market volatility by actively plotting your net profit and losses on a clean interface without risking actual capital. Reddit·r/CryptoCurrency +3
Why Traditional Crypto Sites Hide Their Losses
When hunting for educational resources, it helps to understand why transparent loss logs are so rare:
Conflict of Interest: Major exchange-backed academies are designed to encourage trading volume. Displaying realized net losses works against their primary goal of onboarding new retail investors.
The "Shitcoin" and Emotion Trap: Historical post-mortems of public crypto forums reveal that retail losses are overwhelmingly caused by panic-selling market bottoms and buying speculative "meme coins" at peak pricing. Traditional tutorials gloss over these behavioral pitfalls because teaching dull, long-term asset management generates less platform activity. Yahoo Finance

Are you looking to learn long-term investing (holding) or short-term trading?
Do you prefer written guides/newsletters or video-based courses?
Would you like a recommendation for a completely free simulator to practice tracking your own numbers?
